character: A large resort in Little Cottonwood Canyon just down-canyon from Alta, opened in 1971 and ticketed separately from it. An aerial tram climbs to Hidden Peak, Mineral Basin lies on the back side, and the terrain leans toward steep, high-alpine skiing; snowboarding is allowed.
learning: Reference note: beginner terrain is served by the Chickadee lift near the base area, with Baby Thunder as a common next step; the resort runs its own ski and snowboard school. Confirm current lifts, carpets and lesson products.

prices.note: 2026-27 peak daily ticket: $238 at the window, $215 online. The summaries call the online price a "15% discount", but $215 is about 10% below $238, so one of these figures may be misstated. Dated, variable pricing: non-peak days and advance online purchases (2+ weeks ahead) cost less.

transfers.name: UTA ski bus (Little Cottonwood Canyon service)
transfers.notes: Reference, confirm: Utah Transit Authority has run winter ski-bus service from Salt Lake Valley park-and-ride lots up SR-210 to Snowbird and Alta. 2026-27 routes, schedule, fares and any pass-holder ride benefit are unconfirmed.

transfers.name: Shared or private airport shuttles from SLC
transfers.notes: Reference, confirm: several private operators run airport transfers to the Cottonwood Canyon and Park City resorts. No operator, fare or schedule is on file.

transfers.name: Rental car from SLC
transfers.notes: Reference, confirm: Utah applies a winter traction law in the Cottonwood canyons (SR-210 Little Cottonwood) that can require 4WD/AWD or suitable snow tires/chains. Parking rules for 2026-27 are unknown.
